title: Q-Probe: Scaling Image Quality Assessment to High Resolution via Context-Aware Agentic Probing
claim: Naive zooming in agentic models causes biased or collapsed judgments; context-aware active probing separates true defects from natural effects and wins.
layout: 3 regions: left failure cases (a-d), center ours (e), right pie and radar
description: A wide figure in three parts. The left gray dashed panel stacks four dialogue cases (a-d) in which a user asks an MLLM to rate image quality. Each case shows robot avatars, tool-call boxes with crop coordinates, cropped photo thumbnails of a woman against a dark doorway, and orange-highlighted reasoning text. Sad emoji mark the failures: missed artifacts, ignored face defects, bokeh read as blur, and zoom treated as degradation. The center light-blue panel (e) shows the same task solved by Q-Probe. It follows labeled stages: Global Perception, Local Scrutiny, Background Detection and Critical Thinking. It has a smiley and a lightbulb for correct judgments. The right side holds a colorful icon-labeled pie chart of Vista-Bench scene categories (f). Below it is a radar chart (g) where the orange Q-Probe line encloses all baselines.
caption: Challenges in detecting subtle distortions via global perception versus local zooming. (a) Existing MLLMs fail to capture subtle local artifacts. (b) Even when visible via cropping, Semantic Robustness Bias causes models to ignore defects in key semantic areas (e.g., face). (c-d) Naive zooming leads to Logic Collapse, where the model misinterprets natural bokeh as blur (c) or falsely learns that Zooming implies Low Quality (d). (e) Q-Probe mimics human active viewing (Global Perception $\rightarrow$ Local Scrutiny $\rightarrow$ Critical Thinking) to correctly distinguish artifacts from natural effects. (f-g) Data distribution of the high-resolution Vista-Bench and performance comparison showing Q-Probe's superiority.
abstract: Reinforcement Learning (RL) has empowered Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) to achieve superior human preference alignment in Image Quality Assessment (IQA). However, existing RL-based IQA models typically rely on coarse-grained global views, failing to capture subtle local degradations in high-resolution scenarios. While emerging "Thinking with Images" paradigms enable multi-scale visual perception via zoom-in mechanisms, their direct adaptation to IQA induces spurious "cropping-implies-degradation" biases and misinterprets natural depth-of-field as artifacts. To address these challenges, we propose Q-Probe, the first agentic IQA framework designed to scale IQA to high resolution via context-aware probing. First, we construct Vista-Bench, a pioneering benchmark tailored for fine-grained local degradation analysis in high-resolution IQA settings. Furthermore, we propose a three-stage training paradigm that progressively aligns the model with human preferences, while simultaneously eliminating causal bias through a novel context-aware cropping strategy. Extensive experiments demonstrate that Q-Probe achieves state-of-the-art performance in high-resolution settings while maintaining superior efficacy across resolution scales.
